text: soudarion, -ou, to, (a Lat. word, sudarium, fr. sudor, sweat), a handkerchief, i.e. a cloth for wiping the perspiration from the face and for cleaning the nose: Lk. xix. 20; Acts xix. 12; also used in swathing the head of a corpse [A. V. napkin], Jn. xi. 44; xx. 7.
